evidence: image col. 2: 'ista.in q̄cūq; nō ē mā ñ est aīa.' (in quocumque non est materia non est anima); OCR: 'in quocumque non est materia si est anima'. The negation 'ñ' is clearly printed; 'si' turns the premise of the argument against ensouled heavens into its opposite.

image col. 1: 'p alios eti fit.ß ñ digne ul' rc̄.' (per alios etiam fit, sed non digne vel recte); OCR: 'per alios et fit si digne uel recte'. 'ß ñ' (sed non) read as 'si', so the text now says unworthy ministers act worthily or rightly.

image col. 1: 'expsse fuerit eis ɔmissū' (con-tittle + missum = commissum); OCR: 'expresse fuerit eis omissa'. Parish priests may excommunicate only where it was expressly COMMITTED to them; 'omissa' inverts the condition.

image col. 1 l.3: 'in oībꝫ epl'is pauli ñ inuēies ꝙ excōicauerit nisi tribꝫ uicibꝫ'; OCR: 'in omnibus epistolis pauci inuenies qui excommunicauerit nisi tribus uicibus'. Paul's name and the negation are lost; the claim that in all of Paul's letters he excommunicated only three times becomes a garbled statement about 'few' excommunicators.

image col. 1, foot: 'nō pmittebant hoīeʒ curari in sabbato.& ouē uel bouē trahebant de puteo ī sabbato'; OCR: 'non permittebant homines curari de puteo et sabbato'. An eye-skip between the two 'sabbato's drops the sheep/ox clause and fuses a false sentence (men not allowed to be cured 'from the well').

image col. 1: 'iō necessitate ɔ̄ne nccīuʒ fuit xp̄m pati. ß̄m aūt necessitatē tā aīs ꝙ ɔ̄ns fuit ɔtingēs' (necessitate consequentiae necessarium fuit Christum pati; secundum autem necessitatem tam antecedentis quam consequentis fuit contingens); OCR: 'io necessitatem sine necessitauit fuit christum pati. sed aut necessitate tamen ans quod ans continges'. The scholastic distinction that carries the answer is unrecoverable from the stored text.

image col. 1: '3ª ɔcl'o est ista actualis diui⁹ rerū ñ fuit facta p legē nat'e. nec p diuinam'; OCR: 'actualis diuisio fuit facta per legem nature. nec per diuinam'. 'rerum non' dropped: the conclusion is reversed and contradicts the same paragraph ('per legem nature non… fuit facta per legem positiuam').

image col. 2: 'ipsi de cōmuni ɔcordia inť se diuiserūt' (con-sign = concordia); OCR: 'de communi discordia inter se diuiserunt'. Division by common agreement becomes division by discord — sense reversed.

image col. 2: 'auctoritas ē duplex.s.pāťna & politica… paťna ē iusta ex lege nature.q̄ oēs filii teneńť obedire parētibꝫ'; OCR: 'scilicet pena et politica… pena est iusta ex lege nature'. Paternal authority becomes 'penal' authority twice; the context (sons obeying parents) shows the reading is wrong, but the stored text names a different kind of authority.

image commentary: 'Nā nihil vtili⁹ hoīb⁹ ī hac vita ē q̄ ipa' (nothing is more useful to men in this life than wisdom); OCR: 'Nam nihil vtilius patuit Neque solis viris sed omnibus in hac vita est que ipsa'. 'patuit Neque' is copied from the line above ('vt p⁹ patuit Neqꝫ'), and 'solis viris sed omnibus' replaces 'hominibus'. The words are not on the leaf, but this is a local eye-skip and substitution, not O1 confabulation, and the sense (nothing is more useful than wisdom in this life) survives with only a slight widening.

image: 'Iusticia p⁹ hec ✝tus est' (Martin of Braga, Formula vitae honestae: 'Iustitia post haec virtus est'); OCR: 'Justicia prima hec virtus est'. Justice is the fourth virtue in the treatise; the stored lemma calls it the first.

image l.2: 'Nulli⁹ ip̄rudentiā despicias' (Martin's text: 'nullius imprudentiam despicias'); OCR: 'Nullius prudentiam despicias'. The precept is reversed. The other OCR of this same leaf (b05-r) reads 'imprudentiam' correctly.

image: 'Hec ē vltīa ps h⁹ capituli đ tpantia In q̄ seneca plīma officia tpantie supaddit cū rpetitiōe q̄rūdā phabitoꝝ Et vult pmo ꝙ tu ptinēs firm⁹ eē debes ī disfortunijs'; OCR: 'Hec est uersia presentis capituli et partia. In qua Seneca prima officia proponit. Que debes in disfortunis'. The leaf's text is there, but it is misread ('vltima'→'uersia', 'de temperantia'→'et partia', 'plurima…superaddit cum repetitione'→'prima officia proponit') and a clause ('Et vult primo quod tu continens firmus esse') is dropped (O5). The reader is told Seneca 'sets out the first duties' when this is the last part, adding many more. Serious, but a misread and an omission, not invented text.

image: 'q̄b⁹ aūposit⁹ ꝛ ppo/sit⁹ ē i dignitate sꝫ hūil' vt p⁹ patuit Neqꝫ etiā cōtinēs alic⁹ isipiētiā spnere dꝫ Nā magna mīa'; OCR: 'quibus apposuit et sponsore. Et nam magna misericordia'. The precept (the continent man must be humble in office and must not despise anyone's folly) is silently dropped, so 'Nam magna misericordia est miserere insipientis' no longer supports anything.

image col. 1, foot: 'ꝛ tetan⁹ qñ / scꝫ anteriores ꝛ posteriores ɔ̄tionē patiūt. / in his trib⁹ nō est pfecta cura'; OCR: 'et tetan qn in his tribus non est pfecta cura'. The definition of tetanus (when both front and back nerves contract) is gone, and the two halves are fused into a false sentence.

image col. 2: 'inobediēti⁹ redde/ret. et ideo pdicto mō caute est pcedendum / Cōgruis igiť medicinis'; OCR: 'inobedient redde/ Logruis igit medicinis'. The line is dropped, but it only states the obvious conclusion of the previous sentence (proceed cautiously). No false claim results, and the treatment advice that follows is intact.

image col. 1: 'Uñ heremite dicunť hoīes deserta soli/tudinis appetētes.se ab aspectu hominū se/questrātes'; OCR: 'Un beremite dicunt hoies deserta dominu se questrantes'. 'solitudinis appetentes se ab aspectu homin-' is dropped and fused into 'deserta dominu sequestrantes', so the chapter's definition of hermits (men who seek the solitude of deserts and withdraw from the sight of men) is lost.

image col. 2: 'Fouea aūt intra foueā a late/re ad modū spelunce fodiť i qua cauea que/dam poniť que ad modū cistule preparať.'; OCR: 'Fouea aut intra fouea a late rad modum cistule preparat.' The cave-like pit and the cage are dropped, yet the next sentence relies on them ('ibi i cauea ad hoc parata clauditur').

image col. 1, foot: rubric 'De virgulto / Capl'um. CLXXVI' then 'Virgultū a virga est dictū fm Hug. … pcisum rur/' (about 8 lines); OCR col. 1 ends '…insolentia coercetur.' and col. 2 opens 'sum pullulat'. The <image-desc> even mentions a 'De virgulto' pilcrow, but the heading and the chapter's opening are absent from the body.

image col. 2: 'Itē eis ɔuenit pōpinatio Est aūt pampinare pam/pinos.i.folia supflua de vite amouere vt vue / liberi⁹ aerem purū capiāt.ꝛ foliis nō obum/brate cit⁹ maturescāt'; OCR: 'Item eis evenit popinatio est pinos. id est folia supplua devite amouere et vrue. Visi sunt folia supplua devite non obum bzate cito maturescant'. The line 'liberius aerem purum capiant' is dropped and a phrase is repeated in its place. Real, but the definition (removing superfluous leaves so the unshaded grapes ripen faster) is still recoverable; it is garbled, not reversed.

image l.6–7: 'go aliquid nō est.ergo a pmo si aliqd est aliquid nō est p pdictā regulā Boetij'; OCR: 'go aliquid nō est.ergo ā pmo si aliqd nō est p pdictā regulā'. Dropping 'est aliquid' destroys the inferred conditional (if something is, something is not), which the argument needs for its contradiction.

image: 'Scdō sic.ome totū integrale sequit̄ suas ptes.sed hō mortu⁹ est to/tum integrale ad hoiem.ergo sequit̄.est hō mortuus.ergo est hō'; OCR: 'Scdō sic. omne totū integrale est boiem. ergo sequit.' Major and minor premises are fused into one nonsense premise, and the reply below ('Ad scōm… hō mortuus ⁊ hō ad vocē solū est totū integrale') now answers an argument the reader cannot see.

image: 'ergo semp distinctio fiet circa singularia. ꝛ nunqꝫ circa sensus.quare nulla distinctio erit hic. Decimo sic.ois distinctio cadit sub arte.sed singularia nō cadūt sub arte'; OCR: 'ergo semper distinctio fiet circa singularia. et nunquam cadit sub arte. sed singularia non cadunt sub arte'. The ninth argument's conclusion and the 'Decimo' marker are dropped, and the merged text asserts that distinction never falls under art, the opposite of the tenth argument's major premise.

image right column under '…laus & bonū nomē amittaf.': 'Ericulosae autem: postq̄ de periculis adeundis fecit mentionē: dicit p diuisionē… Laudatq; fabium maximū: qui nunq̄ rumores de se: & infamiam posuit ante patriae sa-' (~13 lines); OCR goes from the text's '…ne nimia quidem facere.' straight to 'luté cu. f. cunctator'. The whole commentary block is missing and the continuation begins mid-word. O5 (it is the page's main commentary, not marginal apparatus).

image: 'Apro. Cōmodis:utilitatibus & bonis externis:qm̄ ipse magnanimus:q circa magna uersaf:non curat bona fortunae:sed nomen & gloriã: citra tñ ignominiã alioꝝ: qm̄ ad gloriã… nati sumus:cum sint uirtutũ praemia. Inuenti aũt sunt:nunc affert illos qui pro patria quicquid habuerunt:& etiã uitã effundere uoluissent'; OCR: 'Apro. Comodis: fed nomen et gloria: citra tn ignominia alioge qm ad gloria et honore et honestate nati fumus: cum uita effundere uoluiffent'. Both drops are real, and the splice yields a false sentence ('we are born for glory… since they had wished to pour out their lives').

image ll.4-7, wrapped around the printed signs: 'Si simile signū [Δ] ꝓpe toralē uel uitæ lineā iuēies / morsū cāis expectato et ma-xime illis i ptibus qbꝰ linee rū-debūt. Tale signū [S-sign] iuxta supmū āgulū si rub℞ fuerit ho-minē cito isirmā-dū dsignabit.' OCR: 'Si simile signum [triangle] apparet orale uel uitae lineae iuxta supremum angulum si rubeum fuerit homine cito infirmabitur. Tale signum [curved line] dū dignabit.' The whole dog-bite clause ('iuenies morsum canis expectato et maxime illis in partibus quibus lineae rumdebunt') is missing, although the margin 'Morsus canis' stands right beside it. The triangle is then joined to the second sign's prognosis (red upper angle → quick illness), and 'prope toralem' is stored as 'apparet orale'. So a reader is told the wrong meaning for the triangle sign.

image, left margin beside the first paragraph: only 'Caue ab / isto hoie' and 'Homici/cide q̄les' (= Homicidae quales). The lower margins have 'Cepha/lea quō formatur', 'Inepti quales.' and 'Caue ab isto hoie'. OCR adds '<margin>Homicidii periculo</margin>', which is on no part of the leaf; the only other marks are show-through from the facing side. So a marginal heading really was invented. But it only restates the adjacent text ('Orbiculi in ea tot ꝓsagunt homicidia'), so a reader learns nothing false about what the text says. It is wrong about the page's apparatus, and the error stays local.

Same leaf as b01-r p.39. Image lines: (5) 'morsū cāis expectato et ma [sign] xime illis i ptibus qbꝰ linee rū' (6) 'debūt. Tale signū [S] iuxta supmū āgulū si rub℞ fuerit ho' (7) 'minē cito isirmā [~] dū dsignabit. Talis uero figura [sign]'. OCR: 'maxime illis in partibus quibus lineæ rui / morfum canis expectato et ma[wavy]iuxta fummum angulum si rubra fuerit homi / debit. Tale fignum [wavy]dici designabit. Talis vero figura [cross] / minē cito ifirmandum'. Every word is present, but the half-lines on each side of the signs are put in the wrong order. 'et ma' runs into 'iuxta summum angulum', 'dū dsignabit' becomes 'dici designabit', and 'minē cito ifirmandum' is cut off after the next sentence. A reader cannot tell which sign means dog-bite and which means quick illness. Strictly this is a reading-order splice around inline figures rather than a single-word misread, but O6 is the closest class (meaning-changing, unrecoverable), so I'm confirming it under that class.

image (zoomed, the 'Undecimo' argument): 'sed ista quoddaȝ aīal nō fuit in / archa noe nō dr multipliciter. ergo nec ista oīe aīal fuit in archa noe'. 'nō' stands clearly before 'fuit'. OCR: 'sed ista quoddam animal fuit in archa noe non dicitur multipliciter'. The negation is dropped. The argument depends on the opposite of 'omne animal fuit' being 'quoddam animal non fuit'. Without the negation, both propositions are affirmative and the topical argument means nothing.

image, col. b, after 'R̷ꝰ q celi ñ sūt animati. rō ē ista.': 'in q̄cūq; nō ē mā ñ est aīa. q oīe aiatū ē ɔpo(situ)m ex mā & forā'. The 'ñ' (non) is plain. OCR: 'in quocunque non est materia si est anima'. 'ñ' is read as 'si', so the major premise (where there is no matter there is no soul), on which the conclusion that the heavens are not animated rests, turns into a dangling conditional with no negation.

image col. a: 'iō necessitate ɔ̄ñe ncciū3 fuit xp̄m pati. ẜm aūt necessitatē tā aīs q̄ ɔ̄ns fuit ɔtingēs' (= ideo necessitate consequentiae necessarium fuit Christum pati; secundum autem necessitatem tam antecedentis quam consequentis fuit contingens). OCR: 'ideo necessitate sine neccesse cur fuit christum pati.sed cum aut necessitate ta antis quam consequentis contingens'. 'ɔ̄ñe' (consequentiae) is read as 'sine', which makes it look as if Christ suffered 'without necessity', and 'necessarium' is garbled into 'neccesse cur'. That loses the response's thesis (necessary by necessity of the consequence, contingent absolutely). The same abbreviation is misread again in col. b, 'nulla ē necitas abso(lu)ta. ẜ tm̄ ɔ̄ñe', which is stored as 'sed tantum ordine'.
